title: One Seamless Workflow With Clo-Set: Planning (Visual Board & Line Sheet)
description:
CLO-SET is a cloud-based platform that enables users to collaborate easily with the entire clothing-making process through 3D file management, sharing, and real-time communication.

Build your mood board on a Visual Board, shape your season lineup on a Linesheet, where a collection goes from idea to plan.

- Visit CLO-SET https://style.clo-set.com/aboutus
- Join Discord: https://discord.com/invite/G2eaK3PDSu
- For any questions, visit https://clo-set-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us
transcript: In this lesson we will learn how to utilize visual board and line sheet in the planning stage of the 3d fashion workflow first we will create a mood board click workspace in the left pane then select visual board click the add new board button in the center enter the title and description then click create once the new board is created click the Edit toolbar on the left to upload reference images the Edit toolbar provides tools for drawing adding text and uploading images for your design you can organize uploaded reference images and by clicking the text button add detailed descriptions in the right pane you can access the closet workflow to browse and use saved 3d assets you can drag and drop assets to add content and choose image views from multiple angles you can further define your mood board concept by utilizing existing 3d material and style assets next we will create color chips using the shape tool in the Edit toolbar select the shape tool and draw a rectangle then choose a file and then select the shape tool and draw a rectangle then choose a file and then fill color from the bubble toolbar at the top you can select colors using the picker or search and apply colors using Pantone color codes once you've found your desired colors apply them to complete your color chips duplicate the rectangle and repeat the process to create color chips in different colors next we'll add simple graphic elements using the pen tool upload a reference image and trace over it to create simple graphics with the pencil tool and pen tool you can freely draw straight lines and Bezier curves allowing you to create your own design references and add them to the board you can also add more visual effects by selecting the color that you'd like to use as a reference or you can also add a background or text for the board once your design is complete arrange it on the mood board you can further enhance your concept by adding multiple image references once your mood board is complete click the slideshow button at the top to view it in presentation mode 3d assets are linked for interactive viewing and you can easily share the your team via a link. Next, we will look at how to plan a seasonal lineup in Line Sheet. First, upload carryover garment files stored on your local drive to the workroom. In the workroom space, click the new button to upload multiple files. You can also copy files from a previous season's workroom. Select the files, click the copy button, then choose the target workroom to duplicate them easily. By selecting the child content option, you can easily track design changes and revisions. To create new items for planning, create blank content. Click the new button and select create blank content to generate style content. Rename the content, then click the Line Sheet button at the top right. In Line Sheet, you can review both newly planned items and carryover products and switch between thumbnail view and list view. It also allows you to manage various content information such as colorway number, carryover status, workflow status, and category. We will update the workflow status and category across the planned products. By updating the workflow status and setting categories, you can finalize the planning stage.
markdown_content: # One Seamless Workflow With Clo-Set: Planning (Visual Board & Line Sheet) This document explains how to use Clo-Set's Visual Board and Line Sheet features in the planning stage of a 3D fashion workflow. It covers creating mood boards with reference images and color chips, adding graphic elements, and organizing seasonal lineups using carryover and new garment content. --- ## Creating a Mood Board in Clo-Set This section details the process of building a mood board using Clo-Set's Visual Board workspace, including uploading reference images, organizing assets, and enhancing the board with color chips and graphic elements. 1. **Accessing the Visual Board** - Click **Workspace** on the left pane, then select **Visual Board**. - Click **Add New Board** in the center, enter a title and description, then click **Create**. 2. **Uploading and Organizing Reference Images** - In the new board, click the **Edit** toolbar on the left. - The Edit toolbar offers tools for drawing, adding text, and uploading images. - Upload reference images to serve as design inspiration. - Organize images visually on the board. - Use the text tool to add detailed descriptions for images or concepts. 3. **Using Saved 3D Assets** - In the right pane, access the **Closet Workflow** to browse saved 3D assets. - Drag and drop 3D assets onto the board. - Choose from multiple image views to showcase different angles. - Incorporate existing 3D material and style assets to define the mood board concept. 4. **Creating Color Chips** - Select the **Shape Tool** from the Edit toolbar and draw a rectangle. - Fill the shape with color using the color picker or by searching with Pantone color codes from the bubble toolbar at the top. - Duplicate rectangles and fill with different colors to build a palette of color chips. 5. **Adding Graphic Elements** - Upload a reference image and use the **Pen Tool** or **Pencil Tool** to trace or freely draw straight lines and Bezier curves. - This allows creation of simple, custom graphic elements to support design references. - Apply desired colors for these graphics to enhance the mood board visually. 6. **Finalizing the Mood Board** - Arrange images, colors, and graphics effectively on the board. - Add backgrounds or text as needed to support the concept. - Click the **Slideshow** button at the top to view the board in presentation mode. - 3D assets remain interactive for viewing from different angles. - Share the mood board easily with team members via a generated link. --- ## Planning a Seasonal Lineup Using Line Sheet This section explains how to organize and manage seasonal garment collections in Clo-Set’s Line Sheet feature, including uploading carryover garments, creating new items, and managing product metadata. 1. **Uploading Carryover Garments** - In the **Workroom** space, click **New** to upload multiple garment files stored locally. - Alternatively, copy files from a previous season’s workroom by selecting them, clicking **Copy**, and choosing the target workroom. - Use the **Child Content** option to track design changes and revisions to carryover garments effectively. 2. **Creating New Items for Planning** - Click **New**, then select **Create Blank Content** to generate new style content for upcoming garments. - Rename the new content appropriately. 3. **Using the Line Sheet Interface** - Click the **Line Sheet** button at the top right to enter the planning view. - Review both newly planned items and carryover products. - Switch between **Thumbnail View** and **List View** for different perspectives on the lineup. 4. **Managing Product Information** - Update various metadata fields such as: - Colorway number - Carryover status - Workflow status - Product category - These fields support detailed organization and tracking of seasonal collections. 5. **Finalizing the Planning Stage** - Update workflow statuses across all planned products to reflect their current stage. - Assign categories to finalize product organization. - These steps complete the preparation for the next phase in the fashion workflow. --- # Summary This workflow with Clo-Set integrates visual mood board creation and detailed line sheet management to support the early stages of 3D fashion design planning. By combining reference imagery, color chips, graphic elements, and organized seasonal lineups, designers and teams can collaborate efficiently and maintain clarity across design revisions and collection planning.
